title: Last charge: opponent reads 'all and each men' as 'all the faithful' and cites Pareus
source_text: CXLII. Unicum restat in quo vir Doctus me calumniae convincere tentat. Nempe in eo quod dixi per Calumniam Reformatis tribui, quod communi consensu doceant, omnes & singulos homines certa fide posse & debere credere sibi fuisse remissa peccata, & se coram Deo justos esse. Et ut intentum suum assequatur, interpretatur mea verba, & conjicit me intelligere per omnes & singulos homines, omnes & singulos fideles. Et postea probat ex Paraeo, hanc esse revera communem Reformatorum doctrinam, quod omnes & singuli fideles debeant & possint certa fide credere se esse coram Deo justos, & sibi fuisse remissa peccata, ac proinde istud citra calumniam Reformatis imputari posse.
pass_a_gloss: One thing remains in which the Learned Man tries to convict me of calumny. Namely in this, that I said it is attributed by Calumny to the Reformed that by common consent they teach that all and each men can and ought by certain faith to believe that their sins have been remitted to them, and that they are just before God. And that he may attain his intent, he interprets my words and conjectures that by all and each men I understand all and each of the faithful. And afterward he proves from Pareus that this is truly the common doctrine of the Reformers, that all and each of the faithful ought and can by certain faith believe that they are just before God and that their sins have been remitted to them — and therefore that this can be imputed to the Reformed without calumny.
pass_b_english: Last calumny charge: Le Blanc said Rome calumniously pins on the Reformed a common-consent teaching that all and each men can and ought by certain faith believe their sins remitted and themselves just.
The opponent re-reads 'all and each men' as 'all the faithful,' then cites Pareus to make that the real Reformed common doctrine — hence not calumny.

lemmas.gloss: all and each of the faithful

rejected: Le Blanc meant only the faithful
